newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called lower after Thursday rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called lower after Thursday rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open lower Friday after staging a modest recovery Thursday and halting a steep decline earlier this week on moderate demand and rising power supply in the West.
"It came off hard from yesterday, but it stablized," said an East Coast power dealer, referring to early over-the-counter (OTC) activity.

July OTC California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $17.35-17.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Thursday's settlement $18.09, while July Palo Verde (PV) at $27.45-27.70 against yesterday's close at $28.17.
Brokers said there were no particular news that pushed the market lower. "It's just a choppy market," said a New York futures broker.
Analysts said July COB and July PV would need to fill price gaps at $19.25-20.25 and $29.00-30.30, respectively, to confirm Thursday's recovery.
Brokers and traders said the power complex would also take cue from natural gas futures. The July Henry Hub natgas contract opened up 1.3 cent at $2.190 per million British thermal units.

Although technical momentum was expected to be sustainable, fundamentals for the Western power market remained bearish as more generation are scheduled to return online and temperatures across the region remain mild.
The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 on the coast of central California and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 near Phoenix, Arizona, both reached full power early Friday after recent outages.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired plant in Wyoming is expected to restart Sunday after being shut for planned maintenance earlier this week, industry sources said.

Meterologists said temperatures in the West would average near to slightly below normal through the weekend. In their six to 10 day outlook, readings across the region would run at to above seasonal levels.
